extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent applicants and practitioners (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive standards for documenting and evaluating patent applications during USPTO examination, including enablement/utility issues, attribution affidavits, file-wrapper handling, and search-record requirements. Oriented to examiners recording searches, handling affidavits/declarations, and maintaining the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility and operability evaluation (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when it is proper to require evidence of utility or operativeness and how to evaluate evidence submitted to overcome a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 for lack of utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2107.02 and MPEP § 2107 - § 2107.03 for utility examination guidelines and overview of legal precedent relevant to the utility requirement of 35 U.S.C. 101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure / enablement (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification must provide an enabling disclosure so one skilled in the art could make and use the claimed invention; once examiner establishes a prima facie case of lack of enablement the burden falls on applicant to present persuasive arguments and suitable proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence supplementing an apparently deficient specification must show the missing information would have been known to those of ordinary skill in the art. Affidavits or declarations aiming to show sufficiency are generally not acceptable to establish facts the specification should recite (see In re Buchner, In re Smyth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight and admissibility of affidavits/declarations re disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations purporting to explain or interpret the disclosure of a pending application are usually not considered; opinion testimony merely stating a claim is 'disclosed' is given no weight unless it explains an underlying factual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per In re Oppenauer and Glaser v. Strickland: opinion testimony that explains the factual basis for its opinion may be admitted and be helpful, but weight is evaluated case-by-case; mere assertions are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution affidavits/declarations (establishing derivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain circumstances an affidavit or declaration may attempt to attribute an activity, reference, or part of a reference to the applicant so that the reference is no longer applicable as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When subject matter disclosed but not claimed in a joint filing is claimed later by S, the joint patent/publication is prior art unless overcome by affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 showing prior invention or an unequivocal declaration by S under 37 CFR 1.132. Designation of authorship/inventorship does not raise a presumption of inventorship; applicants must provide a satisfactory showing (37 CFR 1.132) establishing derivation. An uncontradicted 'unequivocal statement' may be accepted, but contrary evidence can defeat such statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration to disqualify commonly owned patent (37 CFR 1.130)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on a U.S. patent or published U.S. application that is commonly owned and not prior art under 102(b), the applicant/owner may disqualify that patent/publication as prior art by satisfying the conditions of 37 CFR 1.130.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required submissions: (1) terminal disclaimer per 37 CFR 1.321(c); and (2) an oath/declaration stating current common ownership and that the inventor named in the application/patent under reexamination is the prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104. The inventions must not be patentably distinct; the named inventor must have invented the claimed subject matter prior to the actual invention date of the reference. The affidavit/declaration may be signed by inventors, attorney/agent of record, or assignee(s). Limitations: certain foreign dates cannot be used to establish prior invention (see subsections A–C). A U.S. patent that anticipates the claimed subject matter cannot be disqualified under 37 CFR 1.130 or 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of non-permanent papers in the file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that do not become a permanent part of the record should not be entered on the 'Contents' of the file wrapper; papers legally entered are given a paper number and should not be withdrawn or expunged except by Director or as authorized by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.59 allows certain documents to be expunged if unintentionally submitted or containing proprietary information not important to patentability decisions. See MPEP § 724 for petitions to expunge; certain foreign oaths may be returned with a copy retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of papers in the file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: Until revision for allowance, applicant communications (specification, amendments) are fastened to the left side in inverse chronological order; Office actions and other Office communications are fastened to the right side with drawing print kept on top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When duplicate amendments are submitted, duplicate is destroyed except in limited late-receipt situations; at allowance only papers required by the printer are placed in the left side. Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing references are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and endorsement of drawing prints
rubrics_metrics.description: Prints of the drawing are fastened inside the file wrapper by the Office of Initial Patent Examination and white paper prints are kept on top of the papers on the right of the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All prints and inked sketches subsequently filed to be part of the record should be endorsed with the application number of the corresponding application. See MPEP § 608.02(m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of data on file wrapper and PALM bib-data sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner notices an error in data on the file wrapper or PALM bib-data sheet, corrective procedures must be followed according to application series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 08/earlier: correct in red ink on file wrapper and forward to TC technical support to correct PALM; for 09/series: correct in red ink on PALM bib-data sheet and forward to TC for database correction and reprinting; for 10/and above: correct in red ink on file wrapper and forward to TC for PALM database correction and printing of new adhesive file wrapper label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations requiring correction during classification/examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where correction is necessary include correction of inventorship (order/name changes and additions/deletions under 37 CFR 1.48), filing date correction, correction of prior U.S. application number errors, and correction of claims for benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If error is in assignee name or address, it should be corrected by the Assignment Division. See MPEP § 605.04(g), § 202.02, § 201.11 and § 1302.09 for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name or residence changes procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between 'residence' and 'mailing' address; unless applicant requests, residence is not changed on the file; a new residence must be entered into Office electronic records at least nine weeks before publication to appear in a published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a patent to issue with a new residence applicants are strongly encouraged to file an Application Data Sheet (37 CFR 1.76). Patents are printed from documents in the file and Office electronic records; data shown in electronic records other than images are not necessarily relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index of Claims maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Index of Claims' must be kept up to date as a reliable index of all claims standing in an application and the amendment in which the claims are to be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent claims should be designated by encircling the claim number in red ink. Draw a red line below the number corresponding to the number of claims originally presented and further lines to indicate highest numbered claim added by each amendment; cancelations crossed out. Record date and type of each Office action and status of each claim; codes for Office action types are provided. For IFW processing see IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of Search recording (OACS 'Search Notes')
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits the examiner must record in OACS Search Notes the areas searched, the dates of search, and the examiner's initials; in subsequent actions indicate updates and additional fields searched with dates and initials. Search updates should include appropriate databases and the search queries and classifications employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great care is required to indicate places searched and date(s). The record is important for evaluating patent strength/validity (litigation). Searches are separated into 'SEARCHED' and 'SEARCH NOTES' entries per procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCHED' box documentation (classification searches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification searches (complete search of all documents in a subclass) must be recorded in the 'SEARCHED' box with class/subclass, date performed (or updated), and examiner initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is improper to merely list class/subclass without indicating a complete classification search was performed. When updating from a parent application's classification search, record updated searches followed by '(updated from parent S.N. ...)' or 'Pat. N. ...' and recopy pertinent portions of the parent search into the continuing application's file.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCH NOTES' box documentation (limited searches, text searches, consultations, paper searches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries in 'SEARCH NOTES' are intended to complete the record and include limited classification searches, text-only searches, consultations with other examiners, manual (paper) literature searches, and reviews of art cited in parent/related applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited classification searches must be recorded with class/subclass and appropriate annotation, date, and initials. For text-only/database searches record 'See search history printout(s)' with date and initials and include the printout in the file. Consultations: record class/subclass discussed and (optionally) the consulted examiner and art unit. For manual searches record sufficient identification (title, volume, pages, date) to uniquely identify the material. For review of art cited in parent/related applications record the parent application number or patent number with 'refs. checked' or note exceptions if references were not checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search history printout minimum documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any time an electronic search was performed (limited classification or text search) examiners must include a complete search history printout in the application file containing minimum required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum elements: (1) all search logic or chemical structure or sequence(s) used as a database query; (2) all name(s) of the file(s) searched and the database service; (3) the date the search was made or updated; and (4) the examiner's initials. Do not merely list the tool/database name (e.g., 'EAST'). Printouts should be devoid of result printouts to limit bulk. For nucleotide/peptide sequence searches include printouts up to the 'ALIGNMENTS' section. When history commands for particular database services omit some elements, supply missing elements by writing them on the printout or providing portions of the search transcript (e.g., log off command).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking reviewed search statements and limiting printout bulk
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple search statements appear in the history, the statement(s) whose results were reviewed should be indicated; printouts should avoid result printouts to limit bulk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements reviewed should be circled in black ink. A search history printout should be devoid of result printouts; include only necessary history/log information and supply missing metadata when the history command omits elements.
